chunks: He was asked about a Muslim woman who dies, and there is no Muslim woman with her, nor a Muslim man from her relatives, while a Christian woman and Muslim men are present. So he said:
"The Christian woman should perform ghusl (ritual washing) and then wash her."

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُسْلِمَةِ: the Muslim woman who has died
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُ: she performs ghusl (ritual washing) for herself first
key_terms.ذَوِي قَرَابَتِهَا: her male relatives whose presence would affect the ruling
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيَّةٌ: a Christian woman present to carry out the washing

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a Muslim woman dies and only a Christian woman is available to wash her body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the washing of a deceased Muslim woman in a case of necessity when no Muslim woman or male Muslim relative is available. It instructs that a Christian woman should first perform ghusl (ritual washing for herself), then wash the deceased Muslim woman.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.437 - The Imam was asked about a Muslim woman who dies and is accompanied by no Muslim women or male Muslim relatives, but there is Christian woman and Muslim men present.
Imam (as) replied: "The Christian woman should first perform ghusl (ritual washing for herself), and then She should wash the deceased."
